New issue 85 by astuka...@gmail.com: Calculation of the dimensions of tdata
vector variables
http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=85

It's already mentioned on top of TODO file that using tdata block variables
for defining vector dimensions in the same tdata block causes a segfault,
but here's another use case to consider for a workaround:

...

transformed data {
int N;
vector[N] x;

<code to calculate N, doesn't use x>
...
<code to fill x>
}

In my particular use case "x" is an array of input data filtered for
missing values.

I can think of 4 workarounds:
1) delay the initialization of x until its first use, but I guess the
resulting C++ code for the model would look ugly
2) allow variable declaration in the middle of the block, so that x could
be declared when N is already defined
3) allow multiple tdata blocks, .e.g transformed data(1) {}, transformed
data(2) {}, so that block 2 can use variables from block 1
4) in my particular use case I can avoid calculating N, if there would be
support for boolean vectors and R-like constructs y > 0, where y is a real
vector, so that sum(y>0) would give me the number of non-zero entries in y.

Comment #1 on issue 85 by ca...@alias-i.com: Calculation of the dimensions

of tdata vector variables
http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=85

Thanks for the feedback and suggestions. All of them make sense.

(1) would work, but would indeed be very hard to code. I'm not so worried
about the generated code being ugly. That's already ugly and this wouldn't
make it less ugly (arguably it'd make it cleaner if you like your variables
declared by where they're used).

(2) is workable. It won't be straightforward to code given the way the
blocks are parsed now.

We already plan to include compound declaration-definition statements
like "real x <- 0.0;".

(3) is an interesting suggestion. But coding it would bring up the same
issues as (2), and (2) seems cleaner in the sense of being easier to
explain in the doc.

(4) is definitely on the to-do list. In fact, there's already some of the
basic expression template infrastructure in place for it. We want to
vectorize all the unary and binary functions in the MATLAB/R style, not
just the comparison operators.
